status: experimental deployment architecture; no production controller claim
purpose: Record activation, suspension, rollback, resume, and retirement as explicit state transitions bound to exact artifacts, local admission, current policy/authority evidence, health checks, rollback targets, and offline currentness.
invariants: activation is a transition, not a property inferred from installation
every active state is bound to exact artifact digests and one admission record
effect-increasing transitions require fresh authority at transition time
preauthorized fail-safe authority may only suspend, roll back, or retire
rollback target and rollback plan are known before effect-increasing transitions
offline operation cannot perform an effect-increasing transition when required external currentness is unsatisfied
transition receipts are evidence and never become reusable grants
health checks and transition evidence are retained without pretending health proves semantic safety
recovery_rules: suspension should preserve enough state for investigation where policy permits
rollback restores a previously admitted known target, not an arbitrary latest version
resume from suspension requires a fresh effect-increasing transition decision
rolled-back instances re-enter staging before becoming active again
retirement is terminal for that activation lineage; a new deployment uses a new lineage
nonclaims: A successful health check does not prove an artifact is safe.
A transition receipt is not a deployment authority token.
This profile does not define a universal orchestrator or scheduler.
Automated fail-safe rollback is allowed only when preauthorized by local policy.
